  PROBLEM: The contract test hard-codes a narrow scanner that only walks `scripts/*.sh` and `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The docstring and test name claim a "repo-wide contract"; the PR description explicitly calls out fixes in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (which contains 4 `codex exec` sites) and notes latent omissions surfaced in "six more workflows/scripts". The regex `_INVOCATION` plus the file glob therefore cannot catch `*.py` scripts, `*.md` with embedded examples, or future non-`.sh`/`.yml` callers.
  WHY: A future Python helper or workflow variant that adds a standalone `codex exec` without `--skip-git-repo-check` will pass CI but deterministically abort in the worktree workspace (the exact regression the test was written to prevent). The `test_scanner_actually_matches_known_invocations` assertion (>=10 matches) currently passes only because of the limited scope.
